location: Tasks & Acceptance > tests ('`reached` true from only a session `not-run`/`no-slots`/`stopped` record, false without one'); Design Notes > Aggregate
issue: The test bullet drops half of the contract's condition. cell-contract.md > Aggregate sets `reached: false` only for a version that has no record of the session AND has some cell without passing gate-grade evidence. Design Notes > Aggregate says `reached` is emitted for every configured version but never says that a version whose cells all have passing evidence is `reached: true` even with no record in the session. As written, 'false without one' is wrong for an all-passing version, and the test passes for the naive `reached = any record of the session`.
implementation_impact: Headless calls are the usual case here, because each call mints a new session while histories persist. Example: psm-develop calls headless twice on an unchanged module. The second call derives `done` at once and runs nothing. A naive implementation then marks every version `reached: false`, and the return reports every version as `not reached: stopped at done`. The callers then treat a fully proven module as unproven.
suggestion: Reword the test to: `reached` is false only when the version has no record of the session and some cell lacks passing gate-grade evidence; a session `not-run`/`no-slots`/`stopped` record makes it true. Add a case: every cell passes from an earlier session, `--session` is new, no record exists, so `reached: true`. Write the same rule into Design Notes > Aggregate.

location: Design Notes > Docs (stop convergence, Phase 1 loop) vs cell-contract.md > Plan > Stop convergence; plan output fields
issue: The contract's stop-convergence action needs two facts that no plan field provides. (1) The prompt is offered 'where V is not clean or the focus cell has a recorded failure'. (2) The report 'lists ... the failing E2E cells'. `recorded failure` (newest conclusive record of any boot or freshness is a fail) and `failing` (newest cold full conclusive record, fresh or stale, is a fail) are computed only inside the plan. The output exposes neither. A stale failing cell shows rerun reason `stale-source`, not `fail`. A diverging focus cell has a recorded failure but `e2e_warm: false`. The docs cannot rebuild these from `rerun_matrix`, and the interim forbids reading histories directly.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator will guess. It may skip the stop-convergence offer right after a patch: the focus cell is still failing but its reason is now `stale-source`. Its stop report will also leave out failing cells whose records are stale. That breaks the contract's 'lists the failing E2E cells' and under-reports what was not proven.
suggestion: Either add plan output fields `e2e_failing_cells` (list) and `e2e_focus_recorded_failure` (bool), a pure addition with no rule change (check with Budi under Ask First), or name a proxy in Design Notes > Docs. Example proxy: offer the prompt whenever `e2e_step` is `focus`/`cold-version`/`cold-canary` and the focus cell has a rerun entry; report every cell with an e2e rerun entry, grouped by reason. Either way, state the signal so the docs do not reconstruct the predicates by hand.

location: Never (`stopped` records deferred) x Design Notes > Docs (interim rules: exit 143, infra cause keyed on `appended`)
issue: Since `stopped` records are deferred, a child reaped with STOPPED_CODES (143/-15) while ps-run-layer keeps running leaves no record. Its cells are missing from the output line's `appended`, and the run exits 1 (`_e2e_exit`: `child_stopped` gives 1, not 143). None of the kept interim rules covers this run. It is not exit 143, it has no infra cause in `appended`, and it is not a child exit 2. The plan re-derives the same step. `blocked-infra` can never fire, because it counts records and none was written.
implementation_impact: In interactive mode the orchestrator reruns the same step after each such stop: one cold boot per iteration, with no prompt and no loop end. The interim's 'already ran V under this fingerprint' guard is gone too, since the docs replace the interim as a whole. Headless is fine, because the step is not clean and it stops there.
suggestion: Add a docs rule: a run whose `appended` lacks some cells it was given in `--cells`, with no child exit 2 and no `skipped`, is treated like exit 143. Interactive: ask Budi to rerun or end the E2E loop. Headless: the step is not clean. Add a test asserting `appended` and the exit code for a single SIGTERM'd child, so the docs rule has a stable signal.

issue: The generated-history test checks only that no non-canary cell appears outside `gate`/`focus`/`cold-version`. An empty `e2e_next_cells` passes it. So does a `gate` that leaves out some cells, or a `done` derived while a cell lacks passing evidence. The honesty law (tiering never drops a configured cell) and the step definitions are tested only by about a dozen hand-picked I/O rows.
implementation_impact: A derivation bug that drops a cell from `gate` passes AC 1. Examples: excluding `not-run` or `stale-tag` cells, or treating a stale pass as passing. So does one that derives `done` too early. Those cells would never be re-proved before the aggregate, and `ready` would only stay honest by luck.
suggestion: Over the same generated histories, also assert exact next cells per step. `done` holds exactly when every cell has passing gate-grade evidence. `gate` next = every configured cell without passing gate-grade evidence that is not not-gradeable. `focus` = [focus cell]. `cold-canary` = [canary]. `cold-version` = focus version x all configured browsers. Also assert that `e2e_cells_arg` is null exactly when next is empty.

location: Acceptance Criteria #1 (scale) / Code Map ('new pure step derivation')
issue: AC 1 means 4^6 = 4096 combinations x 4 focus-cell variants, about 16k derivations. The AC says 'when the plan derives each' but does not say through which entry point. Through `main()`, each derivation writes six history files, computes the fingerprint and re-imports `ps-e2e-run.py` (via `_e2e_scenario_notes`). The pure function's input shape is not named either: records, corrupt-tail flag, fingerprint, tags, notes, canary, session.
implementation_impact: A literal end-to-end implementation makes the suite take minutes or more. The Verification loop then times out, or someone trims the combinations quietly. A pure function with an unstated signature invites a second derivation path that differs from what `main` runs.
suggestion: State that AC 1 calls the pure derivation in memory and name its signature (per-cell records + corrupt_tail, fingerprint, per-version tag, current notes, canary, session, configured order). Have `main` call that same function, and add one thin `main`-level test for wiring.

location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix (missing rows: canary-version loop-back, non-default canary)
issue: tier-matrix Loop-back has two special cases with no row: 'When V is the canary version, step 2 already covers the canary cell and step 3 is skipped' and 'When the focus cell is the canary itself, step 2 is skipped'. No row covers a tier-1 failure in the canary version, for example 9.1:firefox: warm pass, then `cold-version` [9.1 x2], then straight to `gate` with no `cold-canary`; or a cold full pass, then `cold-canary` [9.1:chromium]. No row uses a non-default canary (e.g. `psm_e2e_canary: 8.1:firefox`) or the default when chromium is not configured.
implementation_impact: An implementation that hard-codes the newest version or chromium in gate composition passes every listed row, since all of them use the default 9.1:chromium canary. So does one that always inserts `cold-canary` after `cold-version`. These are exactly the paths the contract calls out as special.
suggestion: Add rows. (a) Tier-1 fail 9.1:firefox: a warm pass gives `cold-version` [9.1 x2], then `gate` [1.7.8 x2, 8.1 x2]. (b) Canary `8.1:firefox`, clean canary: `gate` = 1.7.8 x2, 8.1:chromium, 9.1 x2. (c) `psm_e2e_browsers: firefox`, empty canary: fresh-module focus [9.1:firefox].

location: Design Notes > Plan ('`--browsers` ... default from `--config`, else `chromium,firefox`'); ps-flashlight-run `apply_config_file`
issue: `CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST` already maps `psm_e2e_browsers` to `browsers`. `apply_config_file` treats a flag as explicit only when its value differs from the argparse default. If `--browsers` follows `--versions` and uses the default `"chromium,firefox"`, an explicit `--browsers chromium,firefox` is overwritten by the config's `chromium,firefox,webkit`. The operator's narrowed scope is widened without notice, against 'explicit flag wins'.
implementation_impact: Projects that configure webkit get extra cells run in scoped sessions, and the scope menu's choice is ignored. This never breaks honesty, but it wastes boots and contradicts the scope the docs say the run uses.
suggestion: Give the plan's `--browsers` an argparse default of None. Fill it from the config's `psm_e2e_browsers` only when it is None, else use `chromium,firefox`. Add a test: config with three engines plus an explicit `--browsers chromium,firefox` keeps the scope at two.

location: Design Notes > Docs > Headless ('`e2e_tier_reached` and `stopped at <step>` come from the plan call that chose the last step run or derived the `blocked-*` step')
issue: The two sources clash after a clean step. Headless judges the `gate` run of a smoke-only module clean (every entry is `not-gradeable`). The next plan call then derives `blocked-not-gradeable`. Both a 'plan call that chose the last step run' (gate, tier 1) and a 'plan call that derived the blocked-* step' (tier null) now exist, and the sentence does not say which wins. Also, `blocked-infra` cannot be reached in headless after any run. Headless stops at the first infra result, and each call mints a new session, so two infra records in one session never happen. The rule's blocked-infra case is dead.
implementation_impact: Different orchestrator runs will report `e2e_tier_reached` as `{1, gate}` or `{null, blocked-not-gradeable}` for the same state, so callers comparing baselines (psm-optimize Verifikasi) see spurious differences.
suggestion: Pin the order: when the last plan call derives a `blocked-*` step, that call is the source; otherwise use the call that chose the last step run. Note that headless only meets `blocked-infra` on its first plan call, which is unreachable with a new session, so test only `blocked-not-gradeable`.

issue: The manual check covers only the positive side: every non-`--merge-only` `--layer e2e` command carries `--tier`. The Runner makes `--tier` together with `--merge-only` an exit 2, and the wrap-up's E2E report-view command is a `--merge-only --layer e2e` call. A docs edit that adds `--tier` to every `--layer e2e` line, a likely mechanical edit, passes the check.
implementation_impact: The interactive and headless wrap-up then fails at the report-view step with exit 2. Headless returns `blocked` (pre-spawn exit 2) after a full validation.
suggestion: Extend the manual check: no `--merge-only` command in the docs carries `--tier`, `--cells`, `--session` or `--versions`. Better, add a small test that greps the reference docs for `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` blocks and asserts `--tier` is present if and only if `--merge-only` is absent.

location: Design Notes > Docs > Headless (config copy: 'resets the canary only when it is well-formed ... and outside the caller's set')
issue: 'Outside the caller's set' does not say how the comparison is normalized. The normalizer trims both parts and lower-cases the browser (`normalize_engines`). A model comparing raw strings judges `9.1:Chromium` or ` 9.1 : chromium` as outside a caller set of {9.1} x {chromium}. It then resets the canary and logs an assumption, even though the plan would accept the value.
implementation_impact: A project that deliberately set a non-default canary (e.g. `8.1:Firefox`) quietly gets the default canary in headless calls whose set contains it. The tier-0 cell, the hosting version and the boot counts then differ between interactive and headless on the same config.
suggestion: State the comparison: trim each part, lower-case the browser, compare the version to the caller's version strings exactly. Reset only when the normalized cell is not in caller versions x caller browsers. Add one docs example with mixed case that is kept.

location: Design Notes > Docs (hosting loop's separate E2E plan call; Phase 2 entry) / Design Notes > Plan (`clean` exit 2)
issue: The spec does not say whether the hosting loop's E2E plan call (run-scope `--versions`/`--browsers`) uses `--per-version`. With `--per-version` over the whole scope, `clean` loads every in-scope version's Layer 1/2/5 files. If one of them passes `plan_layer` but fails the shape gate, every E2E plan call exits 2, including the hosting loop's tier-0 call for an unrelated version. In canonical mode, tier fields are emitted but `rerun`/`phase1_reuse` describe canonical files that exist only after wrap-up.
implementation_impact: The docs authors pick a mode by judgment. With `--per-version`, a malformed file for one version blocks E2E progress for every version. With canonical mode, the call output carries misleading `phase1_reuse: false`. Either way, interactive and headless may differ.
suggestion: State the E2E plan call's exact flags, for example `--versions <scope> --browsers <scope> --per-version`, so it is the same shape as the Phase 2 entry call. Say that its `per_version`/`clean` fields are not read in the hosting loop, and whether a `clean` exit 2 there is handled like any other plan exit 2.
